Treatment effects across the range of baseline risk

Source: R/curve.R
treatment_effect_curve.Rd

Returns the pooled treatment-effect curves on the grid of baseline risk used in the analysis, for example to draw a custom figure or to tabulate effects. plot_treatment_effect() draws the same curves.

Usage

treatment_effect_curve(scale = c("ard", "rmst", "hr"), model = mhspc_model())

Arguments

scale

Effects to return: "ard", the difference in the probability of being alive at 4 years; "rmst", the difference in restricted mean survival time through 4 years, in months; "hr", the hazard ratio for death.

model

An mhspc_model object from mhspc_model().

Value

A data frame with one row per grid point and scale: linear_predictor, baseline_risk (a proportion), scale, estimate, the 95% confidence interval (conf_low, conf_high), and the 95% prediction interval for a new trial population (pred_low, pred_high). Hazard ratios are on the natural scale.

Examples

curve <- treatment_effect_curve("ard")
head(curve)
#>   linear_predictor baseline_risk scale     estimate    conf_low  conf_high
#> 1       -0.7083770     0.1874087   ard -0.009148616 -0.11314296 0.09484573

#> 3       -0.6525567     0.1970319   ard  0.002309064 -0.09183016 0.09644828
#> 4       -0.6246465     0.2020034   ard  0.008037904 -0.08128028 0.09735609
#> 5       -0.5967364     0.2070835   ard  0.013766744 -0.07081767 0.09835116
#> 6       -0.5688262     0.2122737   ard  0.019495585 -0.06045784 0.09944901
#>     pred_low pred_high
#> 1 -0.2374402 0.2191430
#> 2 -0.2208240 0.2139845
#> 3 -0.2043483 0.2089664
